history.period: Founding date DISPUTED: 1840 vs 1909 (both published - unresolved)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the famous Enchey Monastery is NOT in Mangan district - it stands ~3 km north-east of Gangtok in Gangtok district (East Sikkim). Documented with the corrected location. THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (NYINGMA), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. 'Enchey' means 'the solitary monastery'. It was founded by the tantrik Lama Druptob Karpo (Druptab Karpo), a master said to have flying powers who blessed the site after flying from Maenam Hill and established a small gompa/hermitage there. FOUNDING-DATE FLAG: sources genuinely disagree - some give 1840 (Wikipedia infobox) and others 1909 (Wikipedia text) - treat as unresolved. The protecting deities are Khangchendzonga and Yabdean; legend says Guru Padmasambhava subdued spirits here. The prayer hall walls are covered with murals of the four cardinal-direction deities. About 90 Nyingma monks reside here.

name: Enchey Monastery
town: Gangtok (CSV town 'Mangan' is WRONG - the monastery is ~3 km NE of Gangtok)
town_description: Enchey stands on a forested hill ~3 km north-east of Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, with the Kanchenjunga range visible from the complex. It is one of Gangtok's most-visited monasteries, easily combined with the nearby Flower Exhibition Centre and Ganesh Tok viewpoint.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Nyingma) - NOT a Hindu temple

travel.road: Easy road access from Gangtok city (about 3 km); taxis and shared cabs (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to December and March to June; the January-February Chaam is the cultural highlight.
